text.p: Stratasys Inc said Thursday its revenues for the year ended December 31 set a record, rising 122 percent from a year ago to $22.9 million.
"Unit shipments for our flagship product more than doubled over 1995, exceeding expectations," Scott Crump, chairman, said in a statement.
He added that the flagship product, the FDM 1650 benchtop rapid prototyping system, is selling well and the company's consumables sales continue to grow overall.

Crump also said the the initial rollout of Genesys, its 3D-printer, exceeded expectations of the targeted 50 U.S. reseller locations as of the end of 1996. He said the company expects volume shipments in 1997.
"We look forward to adding a highly accurate large output model, the Stratasys FDM-8000, to our family of rapid prototyping products in the second quarter of 1997," Crump said.
He added that Stratasys is launching a variety of new research and development projects that are expected to have a positive future effect and enhance long-term shareholder value.
The company it intends to expense most of these research and development costs as incurred. As a result, Stratasys' earnings in the first half of 1997 may be adversely affected, Crump said.
Stratasys makes rapid prototyping systems for automotive, aerospace, industrial, electronic, medical, and consumer products original equipment manufacturers.
